items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Kirby asked me if I would like to go to California with him... We played a matinee every afternoon... even with me being there a little over one month.

ctx.x: that had helped make Kirby the biggest little band in the world. In place of Russell Procope there was George Johnson, Bill Beason was the drummer and Ram Ramirez had replaced Billy Kyle. When we arrived at the place we were to play (which incidently was a concert) Buster Baily and I found a quiet place and he instructed me on how some of the numbers went. Of course, everything was written and no one that didn't have some experience in reading music could make it in that band and many others for that matter.

I made out alright and a few days later, Kirby asked me if I would like to go to California with him and that was another case of "had horn and would have travel". I had never been in California. I wasn't working and had no great love in New York to hold me there, so it was 'California, here I come' for me.

It was not possible to have pullman service at the time because they were reserved for military personnel and transportation of wounded soldiers and sailors, so we had to be content with making the 5-days trip in reclining seats. We left New York in February, and I really enjoyed the trip because I alwayd did get a kick out of travelling and I had never been further west than Denver, Colorado. I got my one and only view of Las Vegas one night when the train stopped there for about 45 minutes.
